findings.title: Provider-failure handler logs a misleading "unexpected error" traceback and can mask the original error
findings.description:
`_run_part` used to re-raise `ProviderError`, so `execute`'s catch-all produced the single ERROR log. The handler now returns `_exception_result` directly. To keep that log line, it copies `_logger.exception("review: unexpected error in step ...")` into the handler. A named `ProviderError` is not unexpected, and the handler has already logged a WARNING with the artifact path. Each provider failure therefore gets two log lines at different levels, and the second says "unexpected". `dispatch` and `summary` log a named provider failure as one ERROR line with no traceback (`dispatch.py` `_provider_failure`, `summary.py`), so this is also inconsistent with them.

Separately, `effort_sent_by_profile` calls `get_profile`, `ensure_provider_loaded` and `get_provider` inside the `except` block. If any of them raises, the `ProviderError` that explains the failure is replaced, and nothing at that point records the usage. The effort is already known at the start of `_run_part`. Computing it before the `try`, or reading it from the profile the caller already resolved, would avoid the extra lookups on the failure path.

findings.title: LLM spend from the findings-addressed judge is not captured, so run totals undercount
findings.description: `judge_residue_core` calls `run_review_with_profile` without `alias`, and nothing stamps its spend into any `ActionResult`. `LLM_ACTION_TYPES` in `src/squadron/stats/usage_report.py` lists only dispatch, summary, compact and review. `sq stats run` therefore omits the judge's tokens and cost, and the "N of M priced" and "no usage recorded" lines do not mention it. If this is out of scope for slice 175, record it as a known gap in the slice docs or CHANGELOG. As it stands, "totals" can read lower than the real spend with no signal to the reader.

findings.title: Review-client cost resolution bypasses the run's pricing-warning dedup
findings.description: `resolve_cost(alias, ..., set())` passes a fresh `warned` set on every call. `UsageCapture` exists so that each pricing warning fires once per alias per run, and `test_executor_gives_every_step_one_capture` asserts exactly that. Reviews in a looped pipeline step still warn every time, because the review path resolves cost in `review_client` and `record_from_review` then reuses the result. `record_from_error` also recomputes cost from telemetry and ignores the `exc.cost_usd` and `exc.cost_basis` that `review_client` set on the error. The D3 cost precedence is therefore applied in two places for failed reviews. Pass the run's `warned` set into the review path, or have `record_from_error` use `exc.cost_usd` and `exc.cost_basis`.

findings.title: The `"subscription"` cost-tier literal is redefined in the stats views
findings.description: `SUBSCRIPTION_TIER = "subscription"` is a new constant that decides whether a cost is labelled "api-rate equiv." (money or not). The same literal appears in `src/squadron/pipeline/intelligence/pools/strategies.py:39` and `src/squadron/cli/commands/models.py:33`, and `cost_tier` has no shared enum or constant. This breaks the project rule that a comparison value is defined once. Move the tier values to a single definition in `squadron.models.aliases` and import it.

findings.title: `get_all_aliases()` is rebuilt per call on per-row and per-resolution paths
findings.description: `get_all_aliases()` merges the built-in and user alias tables on every call (`aliases.py:217-224`). `_is_subscription` calls it once per rendered row, and `resolver._resolved` now calls it once per resolution. This is probably negligible at current row counts, but loading the table once per render is easy.

findings.title: Broad `AttributeError` catch in the run loader
findings.description: Catching `AttributeError` to cover "top-level value is not an object" is commented and re-raised as a named `RunUsageLoadError`, so it complies with the exception rules. It would be tighter to validate the shape inside `StateManager.load`, so an unrelated `AttributeError` bug cannot be reported as a corrupt file.

findings.title: Usage capture design, SDK telemetry folding, and test coverage
findings.description: `UsageCapture` is the single place a `UsageRecord` is built. `require_capture` fails explicitly rather than skipping capture. The SDK reader (`providers/sdk/usage.py`) validates each value defensively, with a WARNING on malformed input and a real-CLI fixture test. Telemetry is summed over every `ResultMessage`, including injected follow-ups and interrupt drains, and rides `ProviderError.telemetry` on failure. The `except ProviderError` reordering in `DispatchAction.execute` is safe: `ModelResolutionError`, `ModelPoolNotImplemented` and `GitEnvironmentError` are plain `Exception` subclasses, and `DispatchStalledError` is a `ProviderError`, so the stall result now flows through `_provider_failure`. New tests cover success, failure, cancellation, partial records, the missing-capture error, schema back-compat, and the stats CLI and report cores. The 104-character line length in `pyproject.toml` explains the lines over 88 characters.
